title: PriveTAB: Secure and Privacy-Preserving Sharing of Tabular Data
summary: Releases network event data for research by replacing it with synthetic records that keep analytical value, adding t-closeness sampling and SHA-256 encryption of quasi-identifiers on top. CTGAN is the generator: trained on the real data, then sampled repeatedly until the Earth Mover's Distance for every attribute falls below the privacy threshold.
evidence: section '3.1 Generation using CTGAN': we first train a CTGAN model using the real data; after training, the generator in the CTGAN model can generate a sample set used instead of the real dataset

title: Preserving Missing Data Distribution in Synthetic Data
summary: Argues that missingness itself carries information analysts need, which imputation and complete-case analysis both destroy before generation begins, and proposes HottGAN and MergeGAN to preserve the missing-pattern distribution alongside the observable one. Both are built directly on the CTGAN implementation, which is named as the GAN underneath them.
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
evidence: we implement all our methods using Python 3.6.0, PyTorch 1.8.0 and CT-GAN as our GAN implementation; CTGAN employs a conditional generator and the training-by-sampling technique

title: An Empirical Study on the Membership Inference Attack against Tabular Data Synthesis Models
summary: Attacks four tabular synthesizers to see whether an attacker can tell which records trained them, under both black-box and white-box access, then tests whether differentially private training defends them. CTGAN is one of the four victim models trained and attacked, and had to be modified to a Wasserstein loss because its gradient penalty resists DP training.
evidence: we consider CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN and OCT-GAN as our victim models; as computing the gradient penalty of the WGAN-GP loss of CTGAN is challenging with DP algorithms, we change it to the Wasserstein loss and retrain

title: Benchmarking Unsupervised Outlier Detection with Realistic Synthetic Data
summary: Builds an outlier-detection benchmark whose synthetic data is realistic rather than simplistic, fitting distributions to real datasets so that generated outliers deviate in characterisable ways. Vine copulas are one of the two fitted distributions and the one that reconstructs outliers best, letting the benchmark test detectors against deviations in the dependency structure rather than in single attributes.
evidence: Gaussian mixtures yield the best reconstruction of regular instances but the vine is not far from it; compared to regular instances, the Vine seems to perform slightly better for outliers
needs: the vine copula modelling is load-bearing for the benchmark but the implementation is not named; it may be an R vine package rather than the Copulas library

title: SOS: Score-based Oversampling for Tabular Data
summary: Brings score-based generative models to tabular oversampling, redesigning the score network for table records and adding a style-transfer option that oversamples around the class boundary. CTGAN is among the ten baselines it is measured against across six datasets.
evidence: CTGAN has a conditional generator and uses a mode separation process; listed among the GAN baselines in Table 2 and in the full-fake-table synthesis comparison in Table 9

title: Practical GAN-based synthetic IP header trace generation using NetShare
summary: Reformulates packet and flow header generation as a time-series problem rather than a per-epoch tabular one, so that correlations spanning records survive, and adds bitwise IP encoding and parallel fine-tuning for scale. CTGAN is one of the tabular GANs measured against on fidelity and training cost.
evidence: CTGAN appears in the scalability-fidelity comparison of Figure 4 for both UGR16 NetFlow and CAIDA PCAP; prior techniques based on tabular data GANs dominate the synthetic header generation literature

title: Improved Dequantization and Normalization Methods for Tabular Data Pre-Processing in Smart Buildings
summary: Improves how smart-building sensor tables are transformed before a neural network sees them, pairing variational dequantization for discrete features with mode-specific normalization for continuous ones, and reports the gain on thermal comfort classification. Mode-specific normalization is CTGAN's technique, adopted as one of the paper's two proposed transformations.
affiliations: Berkeley College; University of California, Berkeley
Berkeley College; University of California, Berkeley
evidence: the paper proposes mode-specific normalization for continuous features, the transformation introduced by CTGAN, reimplemented as a pre-processing step rather than called from the library

title: Data-Sharing Economy: Value-Addition from Data meets Privacy
summary: Gives data providers attribute-wise knobs to trade privacy against the value a recipient can extract, using two regularizers on a GAN objective rather than obfuscating attributes outright. CTGAN is cited among the generative approaches that preserve statistical properties; the work extends WGAN-GP instead.
evidence: techniques such as Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, Gaussian copula can be used; the paper extends Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty rather than CTGAN
